title: Algorithms at medium scale
summary: A GHZ state on 12 logical qubits, encoded at distance 5 in 839 physical qubits and run through the operating system's interface on a superconducting machine whose control system spans 224 boards.
method: Each algorithm is a logical program. The fault-tolerant compiler lowers it to a QSysASM listing of system calls against the machine's system specification, and its resource VM admits the listing. The OS then executes every system call at its listed time on the control system, and durations the hardware needed enter the next specification until every call fits its window.

The machine is a generated superconducting chip, one transmon per RISC-Q control core, two 4-core decoders, 16,384 words of RAM per core, placed on as many AMD ZCU216 boards as it needs. Every core runs firmware compiled from the listing in the cycle-exact model of RISC-Q; boards exchange measured bits and barriers over their PutLanes.

sections.heading: The programs
sections.text: GHZ state on 12 logical qubits: 12 blocks in |+⟩ joined by a chain of Z⊗Z lattice-surgery merges into a 12-qubit GHZ state, then read out in Z.

findings: The largest run, GHZ state on 12 logical qubits, uses 839 physical qubits and 848 control cores on 224 boards.
Every system call of every program ran inside its window.
